text:
devon: Heads up — vendor SDK upload exposed an AWS access key in S3 object metadata. Found during code review, not in our repos. link: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/vendor-uploads/example.json

alice: ouch. confirmed? do we know the key id?

devon: yes, looks like AKIA...EXAMPLE. object path: s3://vendor-uploads/2026-03-21/payload.json. there's a small block showing it in metadata.

morgan: tagging this P1 for credential exposure. @oncall-sre can you take network/egress containment? also @jordan we should get IAM rotation plan rolling.

oncall-sre: on it. I'll block vendor CIDR in the peering conn and add firewall rule to stop any scheduled outbound from vendor lamdas to our infra.

jordan: IAM plan: revoke the exposed access key immediately, create new restricted key with tighter policy, rotate any dependent roles. I'll coordinate with accounts.

secops-bot: INCIDENT-231: credential-exposure detected — recommended actions: rotate key, audit access logs, enable/verify cloudtrail integrity.

alice: we should assume the key was active for last 48h. start audit: list CloudTrail events referencing that access key, check S3, STS, and ECR calls. Add a watch on suspicious IPs.

morgan: also need to check if vendor encrypted anything with our Vault transit or KMS. vendor said they wrapped secrets with our transit key in the past. if ciphertext left the vendor, rotate wrapping keys.

devon: confirmed vendor used vault transit/encrypt during onboarding. They uploaded wrapped payloads to their bucket. It's unclear if they had the wrapped data plus the plaintext key in metadata — both present in this object.

jordan: coord plan: 1) revoke AWS key 2) new key + policy 3) rotate any vault-wrapping keys used for vendor 4) enable/verify audit log export 5) postmortem. Target: revoke within 10m, new keys in 30m, vault rotate within 2h.

oncall-sre: revoking now:
```bash
aws iam delete-access-key --user-name vendor-svc-account --access-key-id AKIAEXAMPLE
```

oncall-sre: response: 200 OK, key revoked.

alice: good. Jordan — please ensure CI/infra that might be using that key are updated. Put temp deny on vendor role.

jordan: creating new key with minimal privileges and emailing vendor to pick up. rotating attached policies to drop S3:* to only s3:GetObject on specific buckets.

morgan: about Vault transit — recommended path is to introduce a new transit key version and rotate to it, revoke old key for vendor namespace. Steps: create new key version, rewrap any ciphertext that vendor needs (only allowed via rewrap job), then bump key-id used by vendor. We should enforce one-time rewrap and expire old key.

alice: can someone run the Audit log check and snapshot current Vault logs? we need evidence for timeline and for compliance. sample vault commands: 
```bash
# enable audit device if not enabled
vault audit enable file file_path=/var/log/vault_audit.log
# list audit devices
vault audit list
```

secops-bot: Audit exporter status: last-forwarded=2026-03-21T02:12:04Z, backlog=0. If you need longer retention, request via eng-sre.

oncall-sre: firewall rule applied, vendor peering temporarily disabled. No further calls observed from vendor IPs since 1734516802.

jordan: new key created. Sent rotation email to vendor with instructions to pick up new credentials from our secure transfer. Also set IAM credential report and flagged account for rotation.

devon: vendor replies saying they found the plaintext in their own bundling step — they will scrub repo and rotate on their side. Asking whether we still need Vault rewrap.

morgan: yes do Vault rewrap. Even if vendor rotated, any ciphertext created under the previous transit key could be decrypted if attacker had both ciphertext and the old key material. Rotate transit key and rewrap critical blobs.

alice: assign tasks: jordan = IAM & new key policy, morgan = Vault transit rotate + rewrap orchestration, devon = vendor communication & artifacts cleanup, oncall-sre = network containment & logs snapshot, secops-bot = track checklist and remind.

jordan: ETA updates — IAM done, vendor notified. Will post policy diff in #private-secops for review.

morgan: starting vault rotate: creating new key version and scheduling a rewrap job for blobs in path kv-vendor/critical*. Will run in a batch job: 
```bash
# create new key version
vault write -f transit/keys/vendor-wrap/rotate
# rewrap script (pseudo)
for c in $(vault list -format=json kv-vendor/critical | jq -r '.[]'); do
  old=$(vault read -field=ciphertext kv-vendor/critical/$c)
  new=$(vault write -field=ciphertext transit/rewrap ciphertext=$old -wrap-ttl=0)
  vault write kv-vendor/critical/$c ciphertext=$new
done
```

alice: good. please coordinate quiet window with apps team during rewrap to avoid breaking consumers.

oncall-sre: logs snapshot uploaded to case: https://redwood-infra.example/cases/INC-231/logs.

devon: vendor confirmed they scrubbed the metadata and rotated their own keys. asking for a short attestation.

morgan: when rewrap job completes, rotate the transit key again to retire old material and then publish rotation record. I'll post status.

secops-bot: Checklist update: revoke access key ✅, new key provisioned ✅, vendor notified ✅, network containment ✅, vault rewrap in progress.

alice: after action: we need a short postmortem and a preventative item: add a pre-merge linter that scans for credential-like strings in vendor uploads and require encryption-at-rest + metadata policy.

jordan: agreed. I'll add ticket to security backlog and assign to devex for pre-commit hook.

morgan: rewrap done at 1734516890. rotated transit key to new version and marked old version disabled for vendor namespace.

oncall-sre: final check: no suspicious API calls from exposed key after revocation. CloudTrail shows revocation time at 1734516820 and no post-revoke activity.

alice: great work. keep this thread for the postmortem notes. I'll start the draft and ping everyone for edits. :thumbsup:
